title: Exactness and shift compatibility for the external Hom thick reduction
statement:
Fix the finite-field and finite-coefficient datum of [def-trf-admissibility], so \(k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q\), \(\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k\), \(A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\) for a finite extension \(E/\mathbf Q_\ell\) and \(n\geq1\). Let \(X_1,X_2\) be separated finite-type \(k\)-schemes and fix \(L_i\in D^b_{ctf}(X_i,A)\). Use the derived operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and external products and the evaluation-defined comparison \(\beta\) of [def-sf-kv-maps]. Define bifunctors, contravariant in both variables, by
\[
 B(E_1,E_2)=R\mathcal Hom_A(E_1,L_1)\boxtimes_A^L R\mathcal Hom_A(E_2,L_2),\qquad
 T(E_1,E_2)=R\mathcal Hom_A(E_1\boxtimes_A^L E_2,L_1\boxtimes_A^L L_2).
\]
They take values in \(D^b_{ctf}(X_1\times_kX_2,A)\). For each fixed \(E_2\), \(B(-,E_2)\) and \(T(-,E_2)\) are exact functors from the opposite triangulated category \(D^b_{ctf}(X_1,A)^{\mathrm{op}}\); the analogous assertion holds with the two variables exchanged. The natural transformation \(\beta:B\to T\) is compatible with their canonical shift isomorphisms in each variable: if \(c_{B,i,m}:B(E_i[m],E_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}B(E_i,E_j)[-m]\) and \(c_{T,i,m}\) denote these comparisons (with the variables in their original order), then for every \(m\in\mathbf Z\),
\[
 c_{T,i,m}\circ\beta(E_i[m],E_j)=\beta(E_i,E_j)[-m]\circ c_{B,i,m}.
\]
The triangulated structures and exactness have the meaning of [def-weil-triangulated-category]; the comparisons include the tensor symmetry with its Koszul signs.

source.place: first paragraph, sentence beginning “Both sides are exact in each $E_i$”: closure under cones, shifts, sums, and retracts

proof.text: Put $Z=X_1\times_kX_2$ and write $p_i:Z\to X_i$ for the projections. All the internal Homs appearing in $B$ lie in the finite-coefficient $D^b_{ctf}$ categories by [thm-sf-ctf-stability](ii). Apply (i) to $p_1,p_2$ and then (ii) to form each external product, as defined in [def-sf-kv-maps]. This gives $B(E_1,E_2)$, $E_1\boxtimes E_2$, and $L_1\boxtimes L_2$ in the stated categories; a final application of (ii) gives $T(E_1,E_2)$. The projections are separated finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. The same categories have the full inherited triangulated structures by [lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated]. No site-perfectness or dimension-free Hom-amplitude bound is used.

source.place: first paragraph, sentence beginning “Both sides are exact in each $E_i$”: closure under cones, shifts, sums, and retracts

proof.text: At finite coefficients pullback is termwise exact module inverse image by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] and [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Thus it preserves the cone and shift formulas of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For fixed derived $N$, choose a K-flat representative $P$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Tensoring any complex with $P$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms by [def-pc-kflat-complex] and [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]: the cone of a quasi-isomorphism is acyclic and its tensor cone is the cone of the tensor map. The cone comparison is [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso]. On its shifted summand it multiplies by $(-1)^r$ on a tensor factor of degree $r$; substituting the total differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] also identifies the cone projections. Hence the descended fixed-factor tensor functor preserves distinguished cone triangles. It is the derived tensor of [def-weil-derived-tensor]; the symmetry $x⊗y↦(-1)^{|x||y|}y⊗x$ of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] gives the other fixed-factor functor. By the cone definition of distinguished triangles this proves exactness of pullback and tensor in the ambient derived categories.

source.place: Tag 06YM, lemma-derived-tor-exact; fixed K-flat representative and total-cone calculation

proof.text:
For fixed $L$, use [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] to choose one K-injective representative $I$ and put $H(C)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(C,I)$. For a chain map $u:C\to D$, put $V=H(D)$, $W=H(C)$ and $v=H(u):V\to W$. The product formula of [def-pur-hom-complex] gives
$$H(\operatorname{Cone}u)^n=V^n\oplus W^{n-1},\qquad d(x,y)=(d_Vx,d_Wy+(-1)^{n+1}v(x)).$$
Consequently $(x,y)\mapsto((-1)^{n+1}y,x)$ identifies this complex with $\operatorname{Cone}(v)[-1]$: both differentials become $((-1)^nd_Wy-v(x),d_Vx)$. The restriction to $D$ is the second projection $x$; the map induced by $u$ is $v$. The resulting boundary $W^n→H(\operatorname{Cone}u)^{n+1}$ sends $w$ to $(0,(-1)^nw)$; it is $H(-\pi)$ after the inverse Hom shift comparison, shifted by $[1]$. Thus all three arrows are the inverse rotation of the cone triangle of $v$. Thus $H$ carries the opposite cone triangle to a distinguished triangle. By [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] it inverts quasi-isomorphisms in $C$, so the cone-triangle description in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] proves that $R\mathcal Hom(-,L)$ is exact from the opposite ambient derived category. This explicitly supplies the termwise-split argument omitted in Stacks Tag 08JC, label lemma-RHom-triangulated.

For fixed $E_2$, $B(-,E_2)$ is the composite of $R\mathcal Hom(-,L_1)$, pullback by $p_1$, and tensor with $Lp_2^*R\mathcal Hom(E_2,L_2)$. The preceding two steps make this an exact contravariant functor. Likewise $T(-,E_2)$ is the composite of the exact functor $E_1\mapsto Lp_1^*E_1\otimes^LLp_2^*E_2$ with $R\mathcal Hom(-,L_1\boxtimes L_2)$. Interchanging the indices proves the other two exactness assertions. Step 1 puts every vertex back in the full triangulated subcategories, so the ambient distinguished image triangles are distinguished there. Additivity follows directly from the additive tensor, pullback, and Hom formulas; the shift maps are their composites. This is precisely exactness as defined in [def-weil-triangulated-category].

source.place: first paragraph, sentence beginning “Both sides are exact in each $E_i$”: closure under cones, shifts, sums, and retracts

proof.text:
We spell out those shift maps before checking $\beta$. Use $C[m]^r=C^{r+m}$, $d_{C[m]}=(-1)^m d_C$. On the Hom complex a homogeneous map $f$ of degree $a$ is sent by
$$s_m:\mathcal Hom(C[m],I)\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom(C,I)[-m]$$
to $(-1)^{ma}f$, with source components reindexed. Indeed $d(s_m f)=(-1)^{ma+m}d_If-(-1)^{ma+a}f d_C=s_m(df)$. For tensor the comparison $t_{u,v}:P[u]\otimes Q[v]\to(P\otimes Q)[u+v]$ sends a summand of first-factor degree $r$ to $(-1)^{vr}$ times its reindexing; the two differential summands agree by the formula in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Pullback reindexes termwise. These are invertible natural chain maps and yield the canonical comparisons in the statement after localization: existence of the derived Hom shift is [lem-pur-derived-internal-hom-shift-left], and the representative tensor-Hom normalization is [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. In particular the cone calculation in Step 3 uses this same $s_1$, not an unsigned shift.

source.place: opening exactness assertion: canonical Hom and tensor shift comparisons

proof.text: Write $H_i=R\mathcal Hom(E_i,L_i)$. Choose flat-term K-flat $P_i$ representing $E_i$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the specified K-injective $I_i=I(L_i^0)$, and $H_i^\bullet=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_i,I_i)$, so $QH_i^\bullet=H_i$ by the localization factorization of [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]; choose flat-term K-flat $\rho_i:R_i\to H_i^\bullet$. Pullback is termwise [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and preserves flat-term K-flat complexes [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]; hence by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] $R_{12}=\operatorname{Tot}(p_1^{-1}R_1\otimes p_2^{-1}R_2)$, $P_{12}=\operatorname{Tot}(p_1^{-1}P_1\otimes p_2^{-1}P_2)$ and $S_i=\operatorname{Tot}(R_i\otimes P_i)$ represent $H_1\boxtimes H_2$, $E_1\boxtimes E_2$ and $H_i\otimes^LE_i$. By [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] with $\phi=\rho_i$, the evaluation $e_i$ of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] is $Q\psi_i$, $\psi_i(r\otimes x)=\rho_i(r)(x)$, followed by the inverse localized augmentation $QL_i^0\to QI_i$. The reordering of [def-sf-kv-maps](iii) is represented by the chain isomorphism $\sigma:\operatorname{Tot}(R_{12}\otimes P_{12})\to\operatorname{Tot}(p_1^{-1}S_1\otimes p_2^{-1}S_2)$, $(r_1\otimes r_2)\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(-1)^{bp}(r_1\otimes x)\otimes(r_2\otimes y)$, $b=|r_2|$, $p=|x|$: the symmetry of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] with the monoidal pullback comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. So the transpose of $\beta$ is $\varepsilon\circ Q\sigma$, $\varepsilon=Lp_1^*e_1\otimes^LLp_2^*e_2$. Writing $f=\rho_1(r_1)$, $g=\rho_2(r_2)$, $|f|=a$, we abbreviate this as $(-1)^{bp}f(x)\otimes g(y)$; no chain map into $I_1\boxtimes I_2$ or into a model of $L_1\boxtimes L_2$ is asserted. Naturality: replacing $x$ by $u(x')$ gives $f(u(x'))$ on both paths; the same holds for $y$.

source.place: opening exactness assertion: evaluation-defined beta and its naturality

proof.text:
Shift the first variable by any integer $m$. In the homogeneous notation of Step 6 now let $x\in E_1[m]^p$ and $f\in\mathcal Hom(E_1[m],I_1)^a$. The first external-product input comparison $E_1[m]\boxtimes E_2\to(E_1\boxtimes E_2)[m]$ has no sign. The transpose of $c_{T,1,m}\beta(E_1[m],E_2)$ therefore has exponent
$$bp+m(a+b).$$
For the other path, $c_{B,1,m}$ contributes $ma$. After reindexing $x$ has degree $p+m$ in $E_1$, so the evaluation symmetry contributes $b(p+m)$. Its total exponent is
$$ma+b(p+m)=bp+m(a+b).$$
The values $f(x)\otimes g(y)$ agree, including all signs. Thus the two transposed composites agree in the first variable. This is a direct substitution into the evaluation and shift formulas of Steps 5--6.

source.place: opening exactness assertion: first-variable shift square, all integer shifts

proof.text:
Shift the second variable by $m$, taking $y\in E_2[m]^q$, $g\in\mathcal Hom(E_2[m],I_2)^b$, and $|x|=p$, $|f|=a$. Now $E_1\boxtimes E_2[m]\to(E_1\boxtimes E_2)[m]$ contributes $mp$. Hence the exponent for the transpose of $c_{T,2,m}\beta(E_1,E_2[m])$ is
$$bp+m(a+b)+mp.$$
In the other path the Hom comparison on $g$ contributes $mb$, and $H_1\otimes H_2[-m]\to(H_1\otimes H_2)[-m]$ contributes $-ma$. After reindexing $g$ has unshifted Hom degree $b-m$, so its middle symmetry contributes $(b-m)p$. The total is
$$mb-ma+(b-m)p.$$
The difference of these exponents is $2m(a+p)$, an even integer. The evaluated tensors therefore agree. This verifies the second-variable square with its necessary right-factor tensor shift sign; it does not replace that comparison by an unsigned reindexing.

source.place: opening exactness assertion: second-variable shift square, all integer shifts

proof.text:
Fix $m$ and $i$. Model $E_i[m]$ by $P_i[m]$ and $R\mathcal Hom(E_i[m],L_i)$ by $R_i[-m]$ with $\rho_i'=s_m^{-1}\rho_i[-m]$ (Step 5); then $\psi_i'=\psi_i\circ t_{-m,m}$, both being $(-1)^{m|r|}\rho_i(r)(x)$. Shift rule: for $u:K\to R\mathcal Hom(C,M)$, the transpose of $s_m^{-1}\circ u[-m]$ is the transpose of $u$ composed with $t_{-m,m}$. Indeed [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] gives it for $u=Q\rho$, $\rho$ a flat-term K-flat resolution of $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I(M))$, by the same formula; a general $u$ is $Q\rho\circ w$, and transposition is natural in $K$ [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], as is $t$. Compose both sides of the square with $s_m^{-1}$. The $T$-side becomes $R\mathcal Hom(\tau^{-1},1)\circ\beta(E_i[m],E_j)$, $\tau$ the external-product shift; by naturality in the middle variable its transpose is $\varepsilon'\circ Q\sigma'\circ(1\otimes\tau^{-1})$. By the shift rule the $B$-side transpose is $\varepsilon\circ Q\sigma\circ t_{-m,m}\circ(c_{B,i,m}\otimes1)$. Since $\psi_i'=\psi_i t_{-m,m}$, also $\varepsilon'$ is $\varepsilon$ after these chain isomorphisms. Both transposes are thus $\varepsilon\circ Q\chi$ for explicit chain maps $\chi_T,\chi_B$. Steps 7--8 compare their generator signs; they carry the Hom-shift factor $(-1)^{m(a+b)}$ on the $T$-side, equal by the shift rule to the $t_{-m,m}$ factor $(-1)^{m(a+b)}$ put on the $B$-side here. Thus $\chi_T=\chi_B$. Transposition is bijective [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] and $s_m$ invertible, so
$$c_{T,i,m}\circ\beta(E_i[m],E_j)=\beta(E_i,E_j)[-m]\circ c_{B,i,m}$$
for $i=1,2$ and every integer $m$. Other models give the same maps by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] and [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined]. With Steps 1--4 this proves all clauses.
